Subject: Short-term log buffering request for data retention carve-in

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Arbiter is preparing the carve-in schedule for our new integration and we have one operational ask before we sign the DPA addendum: can Redwood hold a short-term log buffer for 45 days for a subset of anonymized request logs while we complete our internal eDiscovery feed recon?

Key constraints: 
- Buffer must be stored in the US region (no cross-border copies).
- Access restricted to Arbiter SOC staff + Redwood support only (audit trail required).
- Buffer must be purgable on 30 days notice once reconciliation is complete (we expect 30–45 days).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
1) provision a temporary retention carve (separate from standard 90-day logs) scoped to our tenant, and
2) provide an SLA for purge-on-request and an audit log showing purge completion?

We’re ready to proceed quickly if legal and privacy align — I can attach a PO once we have confirmation.

Thanks,
Marta

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear summary, and really appreciate the timeline. Looping in Kim (Legal), Karthik (Privacy), and Grace (Customer Ops) so we can confirm feasibility and the purge flow. Quick answers up-front:

- Temporary tenant-scoped buffer: likely yes — we have a temp retention configuration used for a handful of customers during migrations. We'll need to confirm isolation (no cross-border replication) and export controls.
- Purge-on-request SLA: we can commit to an operational purge trigger and confirmation within 72 hours for buffered logs, but legal review may tighten the window or require a signed addendum.

Next steps I propose:
1) Kim/Karthik — can you review the constraints below and flag any legal/privacy blockers?
2) Grace — can your team scope the operational steps (how buffer is created, who has access, how audit events are surfaced) and estimate work hours?
3) Marta — if we can get a PO and sign the DPA addendum, we can spin the buffer up within ~5 business days.

Quick operational notes: the buffer will be a time-limited retention policy applied to a logging slice (no production KVcache or embeddings data). We'll record a dedicated audit event for creation, access, and purge completion.

Hi all — reviewed Marta's ask and Jordan's notes. High-level: we can support a temporary, tenant-scoped log buffer with the following guardrails. I’ve attached a short DPA addendum template (redlined) that covers the scope.

Summary of recommended terms (draft):
- Scope: non-production request logs (request metadata and anonymized URIs) only; no user-generated content or embeddings.
- Location: US-only storage; explicit prohibition on cross-border replication in addendum.
- Retention window: default 45 days max; Arbiter may request earlier purge.
- Purge mechanism: upon Arbiter request Redwood will execute a full-tenant purge of the buffer within 72 hours and provide a signed purge confirmation and corresponding audit records (hash of records removed).
- Access controls: RBAC limited to Arbiter-designated SOC emails + named Redwood ops staff; all accesses logged.
- Evidence: Redwood will provide a purge confirmation PDF and a GDrive link with CSV of audit events for the buffer period.

Open privacy/legal questions for Karthik:
- Do we need a separate DPA clause for transient exceptions to standard log retention?
- Should we require Arbiter to certify that the buffered records don't contain regulated PHI before we accept the buffer?

I’ve attached: dpa_addendum_draft.docx (draft redline) and a short internal runbook excerpt.

If this looks good to Arbiter we can proceed on the PO and finalize signatures.

Kimberly Park
Head of Legal | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai

(attachment: dpa_addendum_draft.docx (docx))
